message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the **presence of a mane** in adult males. While the exact genetics are complex and involve multiple genes and hormonal regulation, the presence of a mane is typically expressed when the dominant allele(s) for mane development are present. In contrast, females lack a mane because they do not carry the dominant alleles required for its expression.
